clinician.trajectory_summary: A 55-year-old male with 30+ years of intravenous heroin addiction, hepatitis B and C co-infection, and hypertension presented with a 6-month history of bilateral hip pain, claudication, decreased muscle power, and soreness of the bilateral lower limbs. Initial imaging workup revealed multiple hot spots on whole-body bone scan (ribs, spine, sacroiliac joint, bilateral femoral neck) and MRI findings of bilateral femoral neck insufficiency fractures, bilateral sacral ala insufficiency fractures, and band-like lesions (Looser zones) at thoracic and lumbar spines—findings pathognomonic for osteomalacia. Laboratory analysis showed elevated alkaline phosphatase (365 U/L), decreased phosphate (1.7 mg/dL), decreased calcium (8.3 mg/dL), and decreased 25-(OH)D3 (24.3 ng/mL in insufficiency range), with elevated urine phosphate (54.7 mg/dL), normal PTH (48.1 pg/mL), normal renal function (creatinine 0.85 mg/dL), and negative FGF23. The biochemical and radiological pattern is consistent with vitamin D deficiency osteomalacia superimposed on osteoporosis, attributed to heroin-induced malnutrition, malabsorption, or reduced sun exposure. Treatment with vitamin D3 and calcium supplementation was initiated. At 6-month follow-up, biochemical recovery was documented: 25-(OH)D3 recovered to 38.3 ng/mL, phosphate to 2.9 mg/dL, and calcium to 8.8 mg/dL, indicating therapeutic response to vitamin D and calcium replacement.
